topic.title: New Orleans: a tanker's rudder jammed on the Mississippi and two minutes later it hit a docked riverboat, which capsized in 22 minutes (NTSB, preliminary)

shape.name: Two clocks
shape.beats: hook: the vehicle at the moment control is lost, named and placed, and the question why it couldn't stop -> the failed part and the first clock -> how it should work (flat diagram) -> what the jammed part did instead -> why there was no stopping (the physics) -> silence, the impact -> the second, slower clock: the consequence -> what is still unknown and a pick-one question -> loop to the first frame
shape.why: a recent accident with a preliminary report: the cause is one stuck part, and the story is two timings the viewer can feel (two minutes to impact, twenty-two to capsize), so two clocks carry the picture

title: Why Couldn't This Mississippi Tanker Stop?
description:
Why couldn't a tanker on the Mississippi at New Orleans stop before it hit a docked riverboat?
Its rudder jammed. We reconstruct it in 3D from the NTSB's preliminary information: the stuck rudder, why a ship can't brake, the riverboat. The cause of the jam is still under investigation.
Sources: NTSB, AP (Nov 2026).
Based on official investigation reports and published sources. 3D scenes are reconstructions, not actual footage.
subject: the Mississippi tanker
